@pytest.mark.parametrize("package, module_name", [
    ("requests.packages.chardet", "sys"),
    ("requests.packages.urllib3", "logging"),
])
def test_standard_library_import_probe(package, module_name):
    # Frozen Python 2 loaders may probe an implicit relative import before
    # trying the absolute name. A missing relative module must not be claimed
    # by a Requests loader, which would prevent the standard-library fallback.

from __future__ import absolute_import

import sys


class VendorAlias(object):

    def __init__(self):
        self._vendor_name = __name__
        self._vendor_pkg = self._vendor_name + "."

    def find_module(self, fullname, path=None):
        if fullname.startswith(self._vendor_pkg):
            return self

    def load_module(self, name):
        # Ensure that this only works for the vendored name
        if not name.startswith(self._vendor_pkg):
            raise ImportError(
                "Cannot import %s, must be a subpackage of '%s'." % (
                    name, self._vendor_name,
                )
            )

        # Check to see if we already have this item in sys.modules, if we do
        # then simply return that.
        if name in sys.modules:
            return sys.modules[name]

        # Check to see if we can import the vendor name
        try:
            # We do this dance here because we want to try and import this
            # module without hitting a recursion error because of a bunch of
            # VendorAlias instances on sys.meta_path
            real_meta_path = sys.meta_path[:]
            try:
                sys.meta_path = [
                    m for m in sys.meta_path
                    if not isinstance(m, VendorAlias)
                ]
                __import__(name)
                module = sys.modules[name]
            finally:
                # Re-add any additions to sys.meta_path that were made while
                # during the import we just did, otherwise things like
                # requests.packages.urllib3.poolmanager will fail.
                for m in sys.meta_path:
                    if m not in real_meta_path:
                        real_meta_path.append(m)

                # Restore sys.meta_path with any new items.
                sys.meta_path = real_meta_path
        except ImportError:
            # We can't import the vendor name, so we'll try to import the
            # "real" name.
            real_name = name[len(self._vendor_pkg):]
            try:
                __import__(real_name)
                module = sys.modules[real_name]
            except ImportError:
                raise ImportError("No module named '%s'" % (name,))

        # If we've gotten here we've found the module we're looking for, either
        # as part of our vendored package, or as the real name, so we'll add
        # it to sys.modules as the vendored name so that we don't have to do
        # the lookup again.
        sys.modules[name] = module

        # Finally, return the loaded module
        return module


sys.meta_path.append(VendorAlias())

import sys


class VendorAlias(object):

    def __init__(self):
        self._vendor_name = __name__
        self._vendor_pkg = self._vendor_name + "."

    def find_module(self, fullname, path=None):
        if fullname.startswith(self._vendor_pkg):
            return self

    def load_module(self, name):
        # Ensure that this only works for the vendored name
        if not name.startswith(self._vendor_pkg):
            raise ImportError(
                "Cannot import %s, must be a subpackage of '%s'." % (
                    name, self._vendor_name,
                )
            )

        # Check to see if we already have this item in sys.modules, if we do
        # then simply return that.
        if name in sys.modules:
            return sys.modules[name]

        # Check to see if we can import the vendor name
        try:
            # We do this dance here because we want to try and import this
            # module without hitting a recursion error because of a bunch of
            # VendorAlias instances on sys.meta_path
            real_meta_path = sys.meta_path[:]
            try:
                sys.meta_path = [
                    m for m in sys.meta_path
                    if not isinstance(m, VendorAlias)
                ]
                __import__(name)
                module = sys.modules[name]
            finally:
                # Re-add any additions to sys.meta_path that were made while
                # during the import we just did, otherwise things like
                # requests.packages.urllib3.poolmanager will fail.
                for m in sys.meta_path:
                    if m not in real_meta_path:
                        real_meta_path.append(m)

                # Restore sys.meta_path with any new items.
                sys.meta_path = real_meta_path
        except ImportError:
            # We can't import the vendor name, so we'll try to import the
            # "real" name.
            real_name = name[len(self._vendor_pkg):]
            try:
                __import__(real_name)
                module = sys.modules[real_name]
            except ImportError:
                raise ImportError("No module named '%s'" % (name,))

        # If we've gotten here we've found the module we're looking for, either
        # as part of our vendored package, or as the real name, so we'll add
        # it to sys.modules as the vendored name so that we don't have to do
        # the lookup again.
        sys.modules[name] = module

        # Finally, return the loaded module
        return module

"""Regression tests for imports of Requests' bundled dependencies."""

import os
import pkgutil
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

import pytest
import requests


@pytest.mark.parametrize("package, module_name", [
    ("requests.packages.chardet", "sys"),
    ("requests.packages.urllib3", "logging"),
])
def test_standard_library_import_probe(package, module_name):
    # Frozen Python 2 loaders may probe an implicit relative import before
    # trying the absolute name. A missing relative module must not be claimed
    # by a Requests loader, which would prevent the standard-library fallback.
    relative_name = package + "." + module_name
    loader = pkgutil.find_loader(relative_name)
    if loader is None:
        module = __import__(module_name)
    else:
        module = loader.load_module(relative_name)
    assert module is __import__(module_name)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("unbundled", [
    (), ("urllib3",), ("chardet",), ("urllib3", "chardet"),
])
def test_bundled_and_unbundled_dependencies(tmpdir, unbundled):
    # Copy the real packages so fallback coverage uses compatible dependency
    # versions and does not depend on what happens to be installed globally.
    root = str(tmpdir)
    package_dir = os.path.join(root, "requests")
    shutil.copytree(os.path.dirname(requests.__file__), package_dir,
                    ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__", "*.pyc"))
    for name in unbundled:
        shutil.move(os.path.join(package_dir, "packages", name),
                    os.path.join(root, name))

    script = """
import os
import sys
import requests
from requests.packages import urllib3, chardet
from requests.packages.urllib3.util import parse_url
from requests.packages.chardet.universaldetector import UniversalDetector

for name in ("urllib3", "chardet"):
    module = getattr(requests.packages, name)
    expected = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), name if name in sys.argv[1:]
                            else os.path.join("requests", "packages", name))
    assert os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(module.__file__)) == expected
    assert sys.modules["requests.packages." + name] is module
    if name in sys.argv[1:]:
        assert __import__(name) is module

assert parse_url("http://example.com/path").host == "example.com"
assert chardet.detect(b"plain ascii")["encoding"] == "ascii"
detector = UniversalDetector()
detector.feed(b"plain ascii")
detector.close()
assert detector.result["encoding"] == "ascii"
assert requests.Request("GET", "http://example.com").prepare().url == "http://example.com/"
"""
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = root
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-c", script] + list(unbundled),
                          cwd=root, env=env)
